Thanks for the sample, Alicia — that helps a lot. Based on the numbers you sent, here's a high-level plan we'll aim to execute during the two-week implementation sprint: 

Week 0 (prep):
- Redwood ingests traffic sample and we run profiler to get sequence distribution and memory footprints.
- We define 3 quantization candidate profiles (perf-first, balanced, fp16-equivalent) to test against your workloads.

Week 1 (canary):
- Canary route for /generate (10% of traffic) with dynamic batching enabled (target batch sizes 16-64 depending on latency SLO).
- KV/prefix cache for common prompts with TTLs starting at 30s; we'll tune TTLs after observing hit rate.
- Validate L4 and L8 quant profiles for throughput/cost; fallback to FP16 for edge cases.

Week 2 (rollout + ops):
- Incremental rollover to 50% then 100% with routing policy tied to p95 latency and error rate thresholds.
- Set up token-level cost dashboards and an auto-fallback policy to a cheaper model variant if p95 degrades >20% for 3 consecutive 5-min windows.

I've attached a short proposal (redwood-tuning-proposal.pdf) that summarizes the recommended quant profiles and routing table we'll try first. Can Monica and Karthik join the kickoff to cover ops and kernel-level tradeoffs?

Jonas

Attachments: redwood-tuning-proposal.pdf (pdf)

Hi all — quick technical notes ahead of Monday's kickoff. These are recommendations, not final: 

- Kernel selection: for your 220-token outputs, GPU memory pressure will be the bigger limiter. We'll start with the optimized fused-attention kernel for sequence lengths up to 512; if we see outlier sequences we switch to the conservative kernel.

- Batching: start with target dynamic batch target 32, max batch 64. Set per-request latency cap 550ms during canary; drop large outlier requests into a low-priority queue.

- Caching: implement a two-tier approach: prefix cache for frequently repeated prompts (TTL 30s -> tune up to 2m based on hit rate) + full-response cache for high-volume templated prompts (TTL 5m). We'll instrument hit-rate and cache-size metrics in Console.

- Quantization profile notes: attached is a short CSV with the candidate profiles (quant-profiles.csv). We'll test L4-fast (lowest memory, some accuracy drift), L8-balanced (recommended start), and fp16 baseline. Our test harness will run A/B evals on a representative prompt set and report quality-delta.

- Routing policy: primary route to high-performance cluster in us-west with dedicated pool; fallback to cost-tier pool (L8) when concurrency >80% or p95 > 480ms for >2 windows. We'll add a Canary flag in the route for easy rollback.

I'll bring up kernel selection knobs and observability dashboards on Monday.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Inference Engineering
